legend: One of the most important products of the R1 company is a popular @r1.com mail service. The R1 mailboxes receive and send millions of emails every day.

Today, the online news thundered with terrible information. The R1 database crashed and almost no data could be saved except for one big string. The developers assume that the string contains the letters of some users of the R1 mail. Recovering letters is a tedious mostly manual work. So before you start this process, it was decided to estimate the difficulty of recovering. Namely, we need to calculate the number of different substrings of the saved string that form correct e-mail addresses.
We assume that valid addresses are only the e-mail addresses which meet the following criteria:
the address should begin with a non-empty sequence of letters, numbers, characters '_', starting with a letter;
then must go a non-empty sequence of letters or numbers;
the address must end with a non-empty sequence of letters.

You got lucky again and the job was entrusted to you! Please note that the substring is several consecutive characters in a string. Two substrings, one consisting of the characters of the string with numbers l1, l1 + 1, l1 + 2, ..., r1 and the other one consisting of the characters of the string with numbers l2, l2 + 1, l2 + 2, ..., r2, are considered distinct if l1 ≠ l2 or r1 ≠ r2.
input: The first and the only line contains the sequence of characters s1s2... sn (1 ≤ n ≤ 106) — the saved string. It is guaranteed that the given string contains only small English letters, digits and characters '.', '_', '@'.
output: Print in a single line the number of substrings that are valid e-mail addresses.
note: In the first test case all the substrings that are correct e-mail addresses begin from one of the letters of the word agapov and end in one of the letters of the word com.
In the second test case note that the e-mail x@x.x is considered twice in the answer. Note that in this example the e-mail entries overlap inside the string.

legend.ai: R1 公司最重要的产品之一是广受欢迎的 @r1.com 邮件服务。R1 邮箱每天都会接收和发送数百万封电子邮件。
今天，网上新闻传来了可怕的消息。R1 的数据库崩溃了，除了一个很长的字符串外，几乎没有任何数据能够保存下来。开发者推测，这个字符串中包含 R1 邮件服务中一些用户的邮件。恢复这些邮件是一项繁琐且主要依靠人工完成的工作。因此，在开始这一过程之前，人们决定先估计恢复工作的难度。具体来说，我们需要计算保存下来的字符串中，能够构成正确电子邮件地址的不同子串数量。
我们认为，只有满足以下条件的电子邮件地址才是有效的：
地址应以一个非空的字母、数字或字符“_”序列开头，且第一个字符必须是字母；
接下来必须是一个非空的字母或数字序列；
地址必须以一个非空的字母序列结尾。
你又一次走运了，这项工作交给了你！请注意，子串是字符串中的若干个连续字符。若两个子串分别由字符串中编号为 l1，l1 + 1，l1 + 2，...，r1 的字符和编号为 l2，l2 + 1，l2 + 2，...，r2 的字符组成，那么当 l1 ≠ l2 或 r1 ≠ r2 时，这两个子串被认为是不同的。

input.ai: 第一行也是唯一一行，包含由字符 s1s2...sn 组成的序列（1 ≤ n ≤ 10^6）——保存的字符串。保证给定字符串仅包含小写英文字母、数字以及字符“.”、“_”、“@”。

output.ai: 请在一行中输出合法电子邮件地址子串的数量。

note.ai: 在第一个测试用例中，所有合法电子邮件地址子串都以单词 agapov 中的某个字母开头，并以单词 com 中的某个字母结尾。
在第二个测试用例中，注意电子邮件地址 x@x.x 在答案中被计算了两次。还要注意，在这个例子中，字符串中的电子邮件地址彼此重叠。
